arxiv-1802-00259.title: Anomaly Detection in Log Data using Graph Databases and Machine Learning to Defend Advanced Persistent Threats
arxiv-1802-00259.creator: Timo Schindler
arxiv-1802-00259.description: Abstract Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs) are a main impendence in cyber security of computer networks. In 2015, a successful breach remains undetected 146 days on average, reported by [ Fi16 ] . With our work we demonstrate a feasible and fast way to analyse real world log data to detect breaches or breach attempts.

arxiv-1803-07134.title: Valence and spin fluctuations in the Mn-doped ferroelectric BaTiO 3
arxiv-1803-07134.creator: Subhasish Mandal, R. E. Cohen, K. Haule
arxiv-1803-07134.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Subhasish Mandal, R. E. Cohen, K. Haule. We study Mn substitution for Ti in BaTiO 3 with and without compensating oxygen vacancies using density functional theory (DFT) in combination with dynamical mean field theory (DMFT). We find strong charge and spin fluctuations. Without compensating oxygen vacancies, the ground state is found to be a quantum superposition of two distinct atomic valences, 3 d 4 and 3 d 5 .

arxiv-2011-11429.description: Abstract Superionic states are phases of matters that can simultaneously exhibit some of the properties of a fluid and of a solid. Superionic states of ice, H 3 O, He-H 2 O or He-NH 3 compounds have been reported in previous works. Silicon, sodium, and hydrogen are abundant elements inside the earth.

arxiv-2203-02956.title: What does it mean to represent? Mental representations as falsifiable memory patterns
arxiv-2203-02956.creator: Eloy Parra-Barrero, Yulia Sandamirskaya
arxiv-2203-02956.description: Abstract Representation is a key notion in neuroscience and artificial intelligence (AI). However, a longstanding philosophical debate highlights that specifying what counts as representation is trickier than it seems. With this brief opinion paper we would like to bring the philosophical problem of representation into attention and provide an implementable solution.

arxiv-2210-13662.title: Analyzing Privacy Leakage in Machine Learning via Multiple Hypothesis Testing: A Lesson From Fano
arxiv-2210-13662.creator: Chuan Guo, Alexandre Sablayrolles, Maziar Sanjabi
arxiv-2210-13662.description: Abstract Differential privacy (DP) is by far the most widely accepted framework for mitigating privacy risks in machine learning. However, exactly how small the privacy parameter ϵ \epsilon needs to be to protect against certain privacy risks in practice is still not well-understood.

arxiv-2304-09803.title: On the Perception of Difficulty: Differences between Humans and AI
arxiv-2304-09803.creator: Philipp Spitzer, Joshua Holstein, Michael Vössing, Niklas Kühl
arxiv-2304-09803.description: Abstract With the increased adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in industry and society, effective human-AI interaction systems are becoming increasingly important. A central challenge in the interaction of humans with AI is the estimation of difficulty for human and AI agents for single task instances.

arxiv-2402-10365.title: Deep Spectral Meshes: Multi-Frequency Facial Mesh Processing with Graph Neural Networks
arxiv-2402-10365.creator: Robert Kosk *, Richard Southern, Lihua You, Shaojun Bian, Willem Kokke, Greg Maguire
arxiv-2402-10365.description: Abstract With the rising popularity of virtual worlds, the importance of data-driven parametric models of 3D meshes has grown rapidly. Numerous applications, such as computer vision, procedural generation, and mesh editing, vastly rely on these models. However, current approaches do not allow for independent editing of deformations at different frequency levels.

arxiv-2410-21764.title: Adaptive Online Mirror Descent for Tchebycheff Scalarization in Multi-Objective Learning
arxiv-2410-21764.creator: Meitong Liu meitong4@illinois.edu, Xiaoyuan Zhang xzhang2523-c@my.cityu.edu.hk, Chulin Xie chulinx2@illinois.edu, Kate Donahue kpd@illinois.edu
arxiv-2410-21764.description: Abstract Multi-objective learning (MOL) aims to learn under multiple potentially conflicting objectives and strike a proper balance. While recent preference-guided MOL methods often rely on additional optimization objectives or constraints, we consider the classic Tchebycheff scalarization (TCH) that naturally allows for locating solutions with user-specified trade-offs.

arxiv-2505-13029.description: Abstract With the development of deep learning, speech enhancement has been greatly optimized in terms of speech quality. Thus, antimicrobial peptide (AMP)-based therapy holds promise as a potential therapeutic approach to overcoming drug resistance.

pmc-12751473.title: Teacher engagement in health profession education: a scoping review
pmc-12751473.creator: Ramya Rathan, Salah Eldin Kassab, Henk G Schmidt, Marloes Nederhand, Andrea Woltman
pmc-12751473.description: IntroductionTeacher engagement (TE) is crucial since it substantially impacts students' academic achievement, personal growth, and general well-being. While extensive research has explored TE in various university settings, there is a noticeable gap in studies focusing on the context of health professions education (HPE).

pmc-13230870.title: Multi-criteria based stable clustering technique for vehicular ad-hoc networks
pmc-13230870.creator: Abdul Waheed Khan, Javed Iqbal Bangash, Shahid Kamal, Zul Hilmi Bin Abdullah
pmc-13230870.description: Vehicular Ad-hoc Network (VANET) plays an important role in the realization of the Intelligent Transportation System (ITS) which leads to a plethora of new applications such as traffic/drivers safety, traffic management, and infotainment. However, the high mobility and dense distribution of the vehicles on the road cause problems for routes management and network scalability.

pmc-13283902.title: Features predicting data exclusion in imaging studies of Alzheimer's disease
pmc-13283902.creator: Shaney Flores, Jalen Scott, Ruijin Lu, Yi Su, Sarah J Keefe, T Hunter Smith, Russ C Hornbeck, Nicole S McKay, Jeremy F Strain, Ashlee Simmons, Kaitlyn Dombrowski, Jacqueline Rizzo, Hope Shimony, Randall J Bateman, Ganesh M Babulal, Susan M Landau, William Jagust, David A Wolk, James Lah, Carey Gleas
pmc-13283902.description: INTRODUCTIONPositron emission tomography (PET) without usable or accompanying magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is typically excluded in quantitative analyses of Alzheimer's disease, potentially limiting study generalizability. We investigated participant features predicting data exclusion in magnetic resonance (MR)‐dependent analyses and evaluated an existing MR‐free PET pipeline to quantify these missing data.

pmc-13332996.description: To characterise patients presenting to a specialised early arthritis clinic (EAC) at a German university rheumatology centre, and to analyse referral patterns, waiting times, pre-referral laboratory completeness, working diagnoses, serological markers, and independent associates of arthritis confirmation and DMARD initiation. Single-centre retrospective analysis of 290 consecutive patients.

pmc-13412410.description: IntroductionIn CheckMate-9DW, the suboptimal early tumor control of nivolumab-ipilimumab resulted in higher early mortality compared with the sorafenib/lenvatinib arm during the first 12 months. Responses were evaluated by RECIST v1.
